comparator.name: Bachelor Civil Engineering
comparator.academicYear: Adopted 2026–2027 ordinary cohort requirements; checked against the completed 7 October audit and current source retrieval on 8 October 2026
comparator.sourceNotes: The controlling 2026–2027 Civil Engineering Annex and September 2026 curriculum chart were verified in the completed 7 October audit. Their ordinary 2026-entry structure is 60+60+60=180. Current year-one Water en Techniek CTB1215-26 replaces the older Schone Watersystemen title/code. Formal Transport en planning CTB1420-25 governs the stale CTB1420-17 chart label. Bouwplaats 1 and 2 are each an aggregate 8 EC; their quarter subdivisions are not separately credited at 8 each. Year three is minor 30 + Surveying and Mapping CTB3310 4 + Urban Water and Environmental Engineering CTB3315 4 + Traffic and Transport Infrastructure CTB3325 4 + one Q3 deep-dive 4 + one Q4 design choice 4 + bachelor project CTB3000-16 10 = 60. Restricted options are instantiated by the first-listed eligible choice in each category: Climate Impacts and Engineering CTB3311 and Design of Water Treatment CTB3465, independently of UCR fit. The old unrestricted three-specialisation arrangement applies only to pre-2024 cohorts. The minor remains genuine choice and must not overlap selected degree/elective units. Fresh current programme-page retrieval corroborates the construction/water/transport identity; fresh formal Annex and chart downloads returned HTTP 502, so formal units, weights and visual verification are explicitly carried from the current-year 7 October audit, not claimed as new retrievals. During the separate UCR reassessment on 10 October 2026, the current formal Annex was successfully retrieved and its ordinary curriculum/choice tables (PDF pp.20–21) visually inspected. These corroborate the existing corrected requirements; the historical download-failure note above refers to 8 October. No programme route, restricted choice or EC value was changed.
components: Genuine choice allowance, subject to applicable approval and overlap rules.

core: Water, flood risk and climate-resilient infrastructure
Environmental systems, resources and sustainable material cycles
Mathematics, statistics and empirical infrastructure modelling
adjacent: Stakeholder needs and infrastructure lifecycle decisions

trace: develops empirical research design and statistical inference before advanced data and economic assessment
provides programming for implementing the target’s evidenced civil/environmental models
develops calculus and differential-equation foundations for quantitative civil/environmental analysis
studies matrix and vector methods needed to formulate linear environmental/infrastructure models
implements numerical equations, integration and differential-equation solvers with error analysis, directly supporting the required numerical-mathematics strand
develops multivariable calculus and differential equations supporting model formulation; it is not a fluid- or structural-mechanics course
develops probability, sampling, estimation and simulation for the target’s probability/statistics and risk-analysis strand
studies engineering and planning that work with natural forces and habitats, including Zeeland examples of human-made flood/coastal interventions
studies flood protection, drainage, freshwater, salinity, subsidence, water infrastructure and decisions about protection and land use
examines recovery and remediation technologies and laboratory/material knowledge for infrastructure resource stewardship; it does not supply structural-material design
uses GIS and earth-observation data for soil/water governance and coastal-protection planning

Field/laboratory soil and aquifer investigation includes applied geophysics, sampling and interpretation. Supports groundwater/site evidence, not foundation bearing-capacity or structural soil-mechanics calculations.
studies coupled hydrosphere, atmosphere and other Earth systems using system modelling, proxies and climate evidence

Aqueous/redox/speciation chemistry, contaminant behaviour, geochemical modelling and laboratory investigations support wastewater treatment and resource recovery; they do not constitute treatment-plant engineering design.
researches resource constraints, geothermal energy, carbon storage and environmental infrastructure questions
establishes planetary boundaries and environmental processes for assessing civil/environmental interventions
develops wave, chemical and materials foundations needed for advanced resource recovery and environmental technologies
studies sea-level rise and climate impacts on construction, transport and society with climate-adaptive spatial-planning responses
evaluates environmental impacts across material/product/process life cycles, directly supporting sustainable infrastructure and lifecycle decisions
Partner-defined small-team sustainability research develops investigation and a report/product/design. No hydraulic design or civil-engineering thesis assignment is guaranteed.

Uses spatial engineering, GIS and remote sensing in disaster, agricultural and environmental projects. Description-only evidence supports real spatial analysis, not hydraulic/structural engineering design.

Develops differential/difference-equation systems, frequency representations, feedback and stability. Actual engineering mathematics and signal-system analysis; no claim of structural statics, fluid mechanics or hydraulic load calculation.

Develops specifications, concept selection, user investigation, production plans and prototypes for consumer products. Genuine design methods and material/circularity inquiry, not civil-structure or hydraulic infrastructure design.

alternatives.label: Water systems, spatial analysis and engineering methods (tested candidate)
alternatives.concept: Test the strongest available combination of delta intervention design, water and soil investigation, environmental treatment, geospatial planning, mathematical systems and product-design methods as a Civil Engineering response.
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum combines environmental/water study with five mathematical courses and data/research tools; it is not labelled as full Civil Engineering.
progression: Each placement is checked against current offerings, earlier formal prerequisites, four courses per term and first-year PPD. Mathematical, statistical and algorithmic foundations were also considered as advisory preferences; limited availability may place some complementary methods together.

candidates.label: Stakeholder needs and infrastructure lifecycle decisions
Road, rail and waterway transport infrastructure

selection.assessment: Mechanically feasible candidate tested and academically rejected: water/environmental inquiry and mathematical/product-design methods do not form a sustained technical infrastructure-design curriculum. No accepted further alternative follows a rejected closest response.

blocks: Tested curriculum and retained external requirements
